/-!
# Erdős Problem 1068

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1068](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1068)
-/

open Cardinal SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos1068

/--
Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain a countable subgraph which is
infinitely connected?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1068 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_  1 →
      ∃ s : Set V, s.Countable ∧ InfinitelyConnected (G.induce s) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1068

reformulations.difference: Lean asks for an induced subgraph on a countable vertex set. The source says 'subgraph', and Bowler–Pitz explicitly say 'countably infinite', whereas Lean has no separate infinitude requirement on the vertex set.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Infinite connectivity is preserved when edges are added: existing simple paths remain distinct and internally disjoint. Thus any suitable subgraph can be replaced by the induced graph on its vertices; conversely, an induced subgraph is a subgraph. Also, InfinitelyConnected requires a nontrivial vertex type and infinitely many distinct simple paths between every distinct pair. A finite graph has only finitely many simple paths, so this predicate already forces infinitely many vertices. Therefore Set.Countable supplies exactly countable infinitude here. Proved the pointwise equivalence with existence of a countably infinite arbitrary subgraph, and the corresponding full quantified equivalence, in /workspace/review/checks.lean. The proofs use only standard axioms, not the sorry-backed problem theorem.
